h: Rescue Stories and Roman Walls by the Broads
p: Redwings was founded in 1984 and has grown into a major horse welfare charity, so every horse, pony and donkey you meet here is part of a much bigger story of rescue and rehabilitation. Visitor centres like this one are a window into that work, and many families come away keen to support it, whether that's by adopting one of the residents or simply spreading the word. Kids often pick a favourite on their first visit and want to come back to check on it.

A couple of polite reminders make the day better for everyone, including the horses. Don't feed them anything you've brought from home, as rescued animals can have delicate digestion or special diets, and always follow any signs about hands over fences. Quiet voices and calm movements go a long way with nervous animals, so it's a nice chance to teach little ones about being gentle around big creatures.

The countryside round here sits at the edge of the Broads and is packed with surprises. Burgh Castle, a short drive away, has the impressive remains of a Roman fort with its mighty flint walls still standing above the marshes where the Rivers Waveney and Yare meet Breydon Water. It's a fabulous, free spot for a walk and a picnic with huge views. Fritton Lake is close too, a wooded stretch of water that's lovely for a quieter wander. Put those together with the horses and you've got a peaceful morning before heading to the seafront for chips.
